clue.text: Farm hand scores over a million in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word for scores is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: scores in the sense of a huge number, a myriad
taken as written

indicators.note: in the end picks the final letter of the word million

explanation.surface: A farm worker earns well over a million by the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' looks like a verb about earnings but means a vast number, and in a down clue 'over' turns it upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who milks cows and tends a dairy herd is a classic kind of farm labourer.

clue.text: Impish type cast its spell (about time) in weird family

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or weird

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters of its spell go around the letter for time
cast as in throwing or moulding, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A magical imp casts a spell, timing it, inside a strange family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as casting a spell but is the anagram signal; 'about' wraps the shuffled letters round the time letter, and 'in' just places the result between the two outer words.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale dwarf who spins straw into gold is the best-known mischievous imp in folklore.

clue.text: Salt, like vinegar, should be cut back slightly

indicators.note: cut back slightly says a little is trimmed from the back, the final letter of the word for sour

parts.note: tart means sharp or sour-tasting, as vinegar is

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: salt, as with vinegar, ought to be used a little more sparingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like the seasoning but is an old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old informal names for a seaman, an experienced sailor being an old salt.

clue.text: Hard to keep wild orgasm in female becoming something else

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the testing word holds the rest

parts.note: trying means hard to put up with, testing

indicators.note: wild suggests out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A racy line about a woman whose wild pleasure turns her into someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' is the adjective trying, as in a trying day; 'wild' shuffles the six letters plus 'in', and 'to keep' wraps the testing word round that and the female letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmogrify is to transform, often in a surprising or comic way, so the word means changing into something else.

clue.text: Staff writer edges away from sea voyage to Italy

indicators.note: edges away from means the outer letters of the voyage word are removed

parts.note: a crossing is a voyage over the sea, such as the Channel
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A journalist on the staff slips off a sea crossing bound for Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff writer' looks like a journalist; the staff is the musical stave, so it is a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini wrote operas such as The Barber of Seville, putting notes on the musical staff.

clue.text: TV's so incisive it excited defenders of animal testing

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: A sharp television programme stirred up supporters of experiments on animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the letters of TV's so incisive it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivisection is surgery on living animals for research, so its advocates support animal experiments.

clue.text: Car feature which is, in fact, minimally used

definitions.text: Car feature which is, in fact, minimally used

parts.words: Car feature which is, in fact, minimally used
parts.note: the feature's abbreviation is AC, the minimal middle of the word fact

explanation.surface: A car accessory that its owner, in reality, hardly ever switches on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rarely used gadget; the trick is that the feature's abbreviation is the middle of 'fact'.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate control that cools a car's cabin is a standard motoring feature.

clue.text: Apparently woman wheels in pet

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
-ess is the suffix that makes a feminine noun, as in lioness; apparently signals the playful reading

explanation.surface: A woman seemingly gets wheeled in as someone's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as CAR-ESS, the answer seems to be a female car; 'Apparently' flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to stroke them fondly, a loving touch.

clue.text: As glue is regularly put in drink it's killing cat

indicators.note: put in tells us the chosen letters go inside the word for a drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, especially of beer

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of As glue, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Glue slipped into a drink turns it into something lethal for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'As glue', and 'put in' drops them in after the first letter of the drink. The cat's name is said to come from a native word for a beast that kills in one leap.
explanation.definitionFit: This big American feline is a powerful predator, a cat that lives by killing its prey.

clue.text: Master said to drink single drink

indicators.note: to drink means to take in, so the spoken word swallows the other pieces

parts.note: oral means spoken, said aloud rather than written
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A master of the house is told to down a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' is the first copy of a document or recording, from which others are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A master copy is the first version, from which duplicates are taken, so it is the source document.

clue.text: Changing this clue in full, I hoped to say "I 'oped"

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the spelled-out clue number and I hoped are rearranged

parts.note: this clue is 10 across, written out in full as words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-referential note: rework this clue so that I hoped becomes the Cockney 'I 'oped'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue in full' is TEN ACROSS; with I HOPED it is rearranged ('Changing'). The definition is by example: saying 'I 'oped' leaves out the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'oped for hoped is the classic case of a speaker leaving off the h sound at the start of words.

clue.text: Bigotry everyone (pay attention) sensed when whipped after S&M

indicators.note: after says the other pieces come behind the letters for S&M

parts.note: S and M stand for sadism and masochism, taken here as letters
all means everyone
to mind is to pay attention, as in mind the gap

indicators.note: whipped as in beaten up like cream, so the letters of sensed are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A lurid tale: bigotry sensed by all once the whipping started after some S&M.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped' rearranges SENSED to EDNESS, the last piece; 'whipped' fits the S&M scene but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow, intolerant thinking is what bigotry is, a closed and petty outlook on others.

clue.text: The Sun or the Earth? One has to go

indicators.note: has to go means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: soil is earth, the ground
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question of which body is central, the Sun or the Earth, since one must be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol is the Latin name for the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman name for the Sun, also used for the Sun in astronomy and science fiction.

clue.text: Facing house of men in solitary

indicators.note: in puts the word for men only inside the word for solitary

parts.note: solitary means single, one
stag describes something for men only, as a stag party

explanation.surface: Someone in solitary confinement faces a house full of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is the theatre audience; an actor in front of them is performing.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor performing in a play stands before the audience, the theatre's house, facing them.

clue.text: Sovereign artefact carried by conveyor belt

indicators.note: carried by means the answer is held within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A royal treasure travels along a factory conveyor belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' reads as a coin, but the artefact is part of a monarch's regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe topped with a cross is part of a monarch's regalia, held at coronations.

clue.text: Measure short nurses for one patient

indicators.note: nurses in the sense of holding close, so the trimmed measure holds the other pieces
short means the measure loses its last letter

parts.note: a scale is a measure, as on a ruler or map
to can mean for, as in a toast to the bride
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A short nurse measures a patient, one of many on the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts SCALE to SCAL, which 'nurses' TO + I. 'nurses' and 'patient' build a hospital scene, but patient is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Being patient means enduring hardship calmly, which is the Stoic ideal of uncomplaining endurance.

clue.text: Genius Paul's partner is shot

parts.note: Art Garfunkel was Paul Simon's partner in Simon and Garfunkel
taken as written
a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A claim that the genius in a famous duo was Paul's partner after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is Paul Simon, whose singing partner was Art Garfunkel.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius can mean great creative skill, so it matches artistic mastery.

clue.text: Ugly one's so flipping quiet

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the Latin word is read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's only links
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: An ugly person is so very quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British intensifier on 'quiet'; it turns ERGO back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being like a hideous giant of fairy tales means being monstrous and unattractive.

clue.text: Financial institution putting up with the public

parts.note: putting up a house is building it
society means people at large, the public

explanation.surface: A bank is said to be tolerating the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up with' reads as tolerating, but 'with' only joins. A building society is a British savings-and-mortgage institution owned by its members.
explanation.definitionFit: These member-owned savings and mortgage lenders are a mainstay of British personal finance.

clue.text: Hoo-ha as United player paid a hooker, ultimately

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names
a pro is a professional, a player who is paid
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of hooker

explanation.surface: A scandal as a United footballer paid a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' could be the rugby position, adding to the sporting scene, but only its last letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a noisy fuss or commotion, a loud public outcry.

clue.text: By feeding John I am without sin, backing faith

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so by is put inside the name

parts.note: Prester John was a legendary Christian king of the Middle Ages
taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so I am goes round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means the word sin is read backwards

explanation.surface: A believer claims to be free of sin, with John nourishing their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, and 'backing' turns 'sin' round. Prester John is a legendary medieval Christian priest-king.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Calvinist Protestant denomination governed by elders, so it names a religious faith.

clue.text: They're not the same bible classes, idiot savant accepts

indicators.note: accepts means the jumbled letters take in the abbreviation for bible classes
idiot suggests foolishly muddled, so the letters of savant are jumbled

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the British school subject

explanation.surface: A gifted but odd savant takes bible classes that are unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'idiot' rearranges SAVANT to VAANTS; RI goes into it ('accepts'). 'idiot savant' reads as one phrase, but 'idiot' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Variants are differing versions of a thing, alternatives which differ from each other.

clue.text: Plain fish without bones

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fish surrounds the doctor

parts.note: tuna is a fish
Bones is slang for a doctor, the nickname of the ship's doctor in Star Trek, so DR

explanation.surface: A cookery note: plain fish served with the bones removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without bones' looks like filleting; 'without' means outside, and Bones is a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain with frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Gives birth to a son on east wing of hospital

indicators.note: on east means placed on the right, the east side, of the hospital letter
a wing of the word hospital is one of its edge letters, here the first

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother has a baby boy in the east wing of the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on east' puts A + S to the right of H, the first letter of 'hospital' ('wing of'); the maternity-ward scene hides the mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a baby is to give birth, so the verb have covers delivering a child.
